title: Chemical Engineering Foundations
description: An explicitly partial university-level survey of chemical engineering foundations: eight routes in six thematic modules spanning process variables and balances, reactive/recycle systems, energy and phase equilibrium, transport, reaction and separation concepts, a synthetic reconciliation lab and an integrated model-audit project. Deeper thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, heat/mass transfer, reaction and separation packages remain future distinct nodes. It is original, unreviewed and formative-only.

modifications: Original readings, generic-species scenarios, synthetic datasets, worked examples, practice, retrieval cards and zero-point cases developed with substantial AI assistance on 2026-11-26. All third-party sources are link-only; no source content, code, figure, table, problem or data imported.

knowledge: General chemistry stoichiometry, equilibrium and thermochemistry
Single-variable calculus, basic data reasoning and careful unit conversion
prerequisites.statement: General Chemistry II and Calculus II are required. Thermodynamics & Transport in Bioengineering, Probability, Biostatistics & Experimental Design, and Laboratory Measurement and Solution Preparation are recommended where the graph permits. Catalog-only thermodynamics, fluid-mechanics and heat-mass-transfer nodes remain separate future deeper packages. These project-planned relationships establish no university equivalency.

outcomes.description: Represent a synthetic process with consistent streams, units, degrees-of-freedom reasoning and material balances.
Analyze reactive and multistream flowsheets, including recycle/bypass/purge and bounded data reconciliation.
Apply first- and second-law concepts and a declared binary K-value flash while auditing model domains.
Explain introductory fluid, heat and mass transfer relationships and their correlation/applicability limits.
Compare ideal batch, CSTR and PFR conversion, selectivity, RTD and nonisothermal model boundaries.
Compare separation mechanisms and quantify recovery, purity and energy trade-offs without design or operating claims.
Audit original synthetic process data with reproducible closure, residual and correlated-record reasoning.
Integrate a conceptual flowsheet and evidence-based model audit without operational or safety approval claims.

lesson_objectives.description: Distinguish BFD and PFD purposes, stream labels and stream-table conventions without treating a diagram as an equipment design.
Apply consistent units and steady total/component balances to a synthetic nonreactive process.
Count unknowns and independent equations for a bounded degrees-of-freedom audit before solving.
Calculate conversion, selectivity and yield for generic species A, B and S while keeping their denominators distinct.
Explain multistream, recycle, bypass and purge balances using explicit boundaries and steady-state assumptions.
Reconcile synthetic process records without confusing correlated rows with independent replicates or missing values with zero.
Distinguish state properties, path quantities and first- and second-law accounting in declared open-system models.
Compute a steady energy-balance term and identify when idealized property and energy models are invalid or incomplete.
Solve a simple binary VLE flash with declared synthetic K values and reject two-phase calculations outside their domain.
Apply fluid continuity and mechanical-energy/friction concepts while distinguishing pump and system curves from equipment sizing.
Compare series resistances, LMTD and NTU ideas for idealized heat-transfer models and analogous mass-transfer resistance concepts.
State geometry, flow-regime, property and correlation-applicability limits before interpreting a transfer calculation.
Use first-order ideal batch, CSTR and PFR balances to calculate conversion under constant declared model parameters.
Relate rate laws and parallel-reaction selectivity to reactor choice without universal performance claims.
Interpret RTD as evidence of nonideal mixing and identify nonisothermal, transport and kinetic-model boundaries.
Contrast equilibrium-stage and rate-based separation concepts across distillation, absorption, extraction, membranes and adsorption.
Calculate recovery, product purity and an ideal extraction fraction with consistent component and total-flow denominators.
Evaluate recovery–purity–energy trade-offs as model-dependent choices rather than operating targets or equipment ratings.
Recompute total and component closure for every row of the original synthetic reconciliation CSV.
Separate measured and reconciled fields, calculate residuals and preserve blank measurements as unknown rather than zero.
Report scenario-level correlated records and model limitations without pooled independence or operational claims.
Assemble a conceptual BFD/PFD and stream-table audit that connects reaction, separation and recycle decisions.
Recompute reactor/separator closure and performance relationships for every synthetic rehearsal scenario.
Complete a five-milestone model audit that documents invalid domains, unknowns, trade-offs and unresolved human review.

modules.title: Process variables, flowsheets, units and material balances

lessons.title: Process variables, flowsheets, units and material balances
lessons.worked_example: A synthetic mixer receives 40 and 60 kg/h, so its steady outlet is 100 kg/h. If the inlet A flows are 20 and 18 kg/h, outlet A is 38 kg/h. Closure checks the declared balance only; it does not establish feasible or safe operation.

modules.title: Multistream and reactive balances, recycle and reconciliation

lessons.title: Multistream and reactive balances, recycle and reconciliation
lessons.worked_example: For a synthetic reactor with 80 kg/h A fed and 20 kg/h A leaving, conversion is 75%. If 60 kg/h A reacts to 36 kg/h B and 24 kg/h S with the declared one-to-one accounting, B selectivity is 60% and B yield on A fed is 45%.

modules.title: State properties, energy balances and binary phase equilibrium

lessons.title: State properties, energy balances and binary phase equilibrium
lessons.worked_example: For the declared synthetic K values K_A = 2.5 and K_B = 0.4 with z_A = 0.6, Rachford–Rice gives V/F = 11/15, x_A = 2/7 and y_A = 5/7. These are algebra outputs, not a real mixture or operating condition.

modules.title: Fluid, heat and mass transfer model concepts

lessons.title: Fluid, heat and mass transfer model concepts
lessons.worked_example: Synthetic terminal temperature differences of 40 and 20 K give LMTD = 20/ln(2) = 28.8539008 K. The value belongs only to the declared ideal exchanger model and supplies no exchanger rating. Always check terminal signs, property bases and correlation applicability.

modules.title: Ideal reactors, selectivity, RTD and model boundaries

lessons.title: Ideal reactors, selectivity, RTD and model boundaries
lessons.worked_example: For a synthetic first-order model with k = 0.2 min⁻¹, a batch time of 10 min gives X = 1 − exp(−2) = 0.8646647. The same k and τ = 5 min give CSTR X = 0.5 and PFR X = 1 − exp(−1) = 0.6321206.

modules.title: Separations, process reconciliation and integrated model audit

lessons.title: Separation concepts and recovery–purity–energy trade-offs
lessons.worked_example: If 100 kg/h A enters a fictional separator and 80 kg/h A reports to a 100 kg/h product, A recovery is 80% and product A purity is 80%. Neither percentage proves separation feasibility, product quality or energy performance.

lessons.title: Original synthetic process-reconciliation lab
lessons.worked_example: LAB-01 has feed A flows 20 and 18 kg/h, so reconciled product A is 38 kg/h even though its synthetic measured field is 41. LAB-02 has a 102 − 100 = 2 kg/h total residual. Reused scenario rows are correlated, not independent replicates.

lessons.title: Integrated conceptual flowsheet and model-audit project
lessons.worked_example: R01 forms 42 kg/h B and recovers fraction 0.90, so recovered B is 37.8 kg/h. R02 selectivity is 48/(48+24)×100 = 66.6667%; R03 recovered-B yield on feed A is 24/90×100 = 26.6667%. R04 recovery remains unknown.

grading_policy.attempt_policy: Unlimited formative retries; no summative grade is awarded.
grading_policy.solution_release: Public practice solutions may be shown after an attempt; case checklists are zero-point self-assessments.
grading_policy.late_policy: No deadlines or late penalties exist in this partial package.
grading_policy.appeals: No instructor review workflow is implemented; report ambiguous items as content issues.

accessibility.diagram_policy: No copied figures or embedded diagrams are included; BFD/PFD, stream and model relationships are expressed in prose, equations and original tables.
known_issues: Unicode subscripts, superscripts, Greek letters and equations require structured alternatives and assistive-technology review.
CSV tables and text-based flowsheet descriptions have not undergone accessibility or usability review.

history.summary: New explicitly partial university-level chemical engineering survey: eight routes in six modules, eight original substantive readings, 48 public practice items worth 56 points, 24 retrieval cards, two original synthetic CSVs, one zero-point integrative case and five zero-point project milestones. All third-party sources are link-only; no operational design, recipe, equipment rating or safety approval is supplied.

limitations: This eight-route, six-module package is an explicitly partial university-level survey, not a complete or measured course. It is unreviewed and formative-only; no competency, credit, qualification or institutional authorization is established.

All processes, species A/B/S, scenarios, measurements and CSV rows are original synthetic teaching constructions. Arithmetic closure is not proof of safe or feasible operation, experimental validation or engineering approval.

No real production recipe, chemical identifier, hazardous operational condition, plant operating target, controller setting, line or pump sizing, equipment rating or relief sizing is supplied. No safety, release or operating approval is granted.

Catalog-only thermodynamics, fluid-mechanics and heat-mass-transfer nodes are not promoted. Full property methods, fluid mechanics, transport, reaction engineering, separations, process control, safety and design remain future distinct packages.
VLE uses declared synthetic constant K values only. It is not a real mixture model, phase-data prediction or general flash solver; two-phase and physical-domain checks are mandatory.

Fluid, exchanger, reactor and separator examples use bounded ideal models. They provide no detailed design, scale-up, equipment selection, correlation validation, process safety or operability assessment.

Rows reused within a lab scenario are correlated records, not independent replicates. Reconciliation is deterministic closure practice, not uncertainty quantification or statistical independence evidence; missing values remain unknown and never become zero.

Of the 24 numerical answers, 0 require units, 0 check significant figures and 0 check dimensions. Every numeric key has an authored absolute tolerance and independent arithmetic/misconception tests; learners must still show units and derivations.

No numeric question uses authored randomization variants in version 0.1.0; all 24 base numeric keys and all public CSV conservation/closure relationships are independently recomputed by the package tests.

Official MIT and reused chemistry, transport, statistics and control records are link-only. No third-party prose, figure, table, problem, dataset or asset is imported, and no endorsement or qualified review is implied.
intentionally_omitted: Real chemicals, production recipes, hazardous conditions, operating targets, controller settings and plant instructions.
Line/pump sizing, equipment ratings, relief sizing, detailed mechanical design, operability review and safety/release approval.
Promotion or full coverage of catalog-only thermodynamics, fluid mechanics and heat/mass transfer; advanced reaction, separation, control and process-design packages.
Physical experiments, real process data, uncertainty-qualified reconciliation, independent replication and measured workload.
Graded assessment, qualified scientific/engineering review and claims of university equivalence or professional competence.
